text:
mike-infra: seeing a spike of model-pull failures in eu-west1 since ~03:20 UTC, pods getting 503/connection reset when fetching artifacts. rolling back a few tasks shows same behavior. not CPU/memory. suspect sidecar/egress policy.

sam-oncall: can you paste envoy/egress-gateway logs and a failing curl from a pod? any DNS errors? @sam-oncall responding live

mike-infra: paste logs below. short snippets — envoy shows upstream reset, egress gateway returning 502 occasionally. from app pod: 
```
curl -v https://models.internal.redwood/eu-west/model.tar.gz
* Connected to models.internal.redwood (10.12.3.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake ok
* Connected and then immediately: "Connection reset by peer"
* Closing connection 0
```
envoy: "upstream reset before response complete" x200 over 10m. no auth failures.

joy-ml: we're seeing failed downloads for both hosted and dedicated instances, so not just one pool. embedding jobs are queuing. errors appear right after kube-probe restarts on those nodes.

carol-platform: any recent change to egress allowlists or the egress-gateway policy for eu-west1? last PR (infra#872) tightened outbound to only allow 443 via egress-gateway and blocked other outbound except cluster-dns. that might block kubelet/probes or health-targets that use ephemeral ports.

mike-infra: yes PR merged yesterday. I think liveness/readiness probes or sidecar healthchecks that reach node-local endpoints are getting routed through the egress gateway and rejected. see this from a sidecar: 
```
[2026-03-18T03:21:10Z] environment: outbound|tcp|10.12.3.1:10250 to egress-gateway
upstream response: 403 denied by policy
```

sam-oncall: if probes are being proxied through the gateway, kubelet may drop the pod or restart containers, which could cause transient connection churn and ephemeral port/NAT pressure. can you confirm if nodes are hitting SNAT port exhaustion? metrics?

mike-infra: net/nat_ports graph spiked, conntrack count high on those nodepools. ephemeral ports used up quickly when many pods restart and all traffic flows through a single egress gateway IP.

carol-platform: temporary mitigation: exclude probe traffic from sidecar egress. two options: 1) annotate pods that run downloads with hostNetwork: true for probes (not great) or 2) add an exclusion to sidecar egress policy to allow node CIDR and kubelet ports (10250/10255) and health endpoints, or 3) add the nodepool to the egress-gateway static NAT pool so SNAT scales.

joy-ml: can we do a quick patch to egress policy to allow node CIDR and kubelet ports in eu-west1? low blast radius.

mike-infra: proposing small PR to union in node CIDR (10.12.0.0/16) and allow tcp:10250,tcp:10255 and UDP 53 to coreDNS explicitly. will push canary. patch example: 
```
# egress policy snippet
- to:
  - cidr: 10.12.0.0/16
    ports: [10250,10255]
  - service: kube-dns.kube-system.svc.cluster.local
    ports: [53]
```
annotate example fallback for a pod: `traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeOutboundIPRanges: 10.12.0.0/16` for quick emergency bypass.

sam-oncall: go ahead with the canary change for eu-west1 only, monitor SNAT, envoy 5xx, and model-pull success rate. keep deploy-bot in loop.

deploy-bot: started canary patch in eu-west1 (pool: models-prod-eu-1), hash infra#872-hotfix-1902. canary target: 10 pods.

mike-infra: canary logs look good so far (10m). model pulls succeeded on the canary pods. envoy upstream 5xx dropped to 0 on those nodes.

ingress-bot: alert cleared: egress-gateway 502 incidents reduced for eu-west1.

joy-ml: thanks! embedding backlog draining. any plan to avoid recurrence?

carol-platform: long term: we should (a) expand egress-gateway SNAT capacity or add per-node egress to reduce single IP pressure, (b) update our default egress policy runbook to explicitly allow kubelet/probe flows, and (c) add tests that simulate probe-heavy churn to catch this in staging. opening infra#879 with details and a postmortem template.

mike-infra: will add runbook patch and a short blameless postmortem. for now we've rolled the canary to full eu-west1 and restored normal model pulls. follow-ups: increase NAT port pool for egress-gateway, add probe exclusion annotation docs, and add automated test.

sam-oncall: closing the immediate incident, marking follow-ups in infra#879. nice quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
